THE QUESTION

What does latent prediction actually show?

JEPA predicts representations rather than reconstructing every pixel. That learning objective can produce useful features, but a method's world-model capability depends on what its experiments test.

This survey uses two complementary views: a five-family taxonomy for the methods, and four capability levels for the evidence reported in their original studies.

01 / METHOD TAXONOMY

Five JEPA families

Organized by the main prediction task. A method may span several families; the survey places it by its principal contribution.

01
F

Foundational / static

Predict missing representations from context within a static observation.

JEPA-F
02
T

Temporal

Learn from video and predict representations across time or toward future states.

JEPA-T
03
A

Action-conditioned

Condition latent-state prediction on actions to model their possible effects.

JEPA-A
04
M

Multimodal

Use latent prediction to connect images, language, audio, or other sensors.

JEPA-M
05
SC

Structured / scene-centric

Predict representations that preserve points, objects, geometry, or relations.

JEPA-SC

02 / EVIDENCE LENS

Four capability levels

These levels describe what the reported evaluations support. A taxonomy label alone does not establish a capability.

R

Representation

Are the learned features useful?

P

Prediction

Can the model predict states not yet observed?

I

Intervention

Does prediction respond to changed actions?

C

Control

Does the complete system use prediction in a feedback loop?
